The experiments (sweep k, vary workload domain and batch size) are classic, well-scoped, and runnable on a single GPU with small 1B-3B models. Its learning order even includes correctness testing and simple profiling. Both answers are specific and current, but B's realistic success criterion (a verified ~1.3-2x speedup with honest overhead analysis) is achievable, whereas A's 'contribute a reproducible harness filling a gap' and vLLM-internals work is riskier for a first-time researcher meeting a supervisor only bi-weekly.

Answer A is calibrated to this exact person: a PyTorch-basics undergrad with one rented GPU, no research experience, 10-12 weeks. It also sets realistic expectations (1.3-2x batch-1 speedup) and gives a safe fallback (HF built-in spec decode as a sanity check, not a replication target). Every first step is doable this week on a laptop plus one GPU with 1-3B models.
